latest_evidence.probe: When a deterministic effect resource can be deleted, what is the minimum durable identity-retention contract that still blocks an ambiguous-success retry from duplicating the effect? Compare immutable tombstone, generation/version namespace, and separate completion-token retention.
latest_evidence.tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification using only frozen CLEAN authority, own role-local LATEST state, and RFC 9110; no external effect, hosted compute, paid/trial API, protected authority, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, manual execution, scheduler mutation, or quota-bearing service.
latest_evidence.semantic_conclusion: After deletion, current-resource existence no longer preserves deterministic identity against arbitrary replay. The minimum safe contract is a durable non-reusable operation-identity marker retained until replay is provably impossible; if no finite replay bound is proven, retention/nonreuse must be indefinite. A generation/version namespace alone fails unless used identities remain durably reserved. A separate completion token is equivalent to a tombstone when stable, non-reusable, authoritative, and atomically bound. Hidden/non-resource side effects require atomic coupling or independent idempotence.

candidate_comparison.immutable_tombstone: best overall: low expected completion time, high duplicate safety under retention+atomic-binding assumptions, low-to-medium integration cost
candidate_comparison.completion_token_retention: high safety but medium integration cost due separate token/effect binding

latest_evidence.conflict_check: Exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child; own role-local state plus public RFC only; no scheduler mutation, wait/poll/backoff/retry or optional second leaf.
